units.source_text: 且说左大将髭黑的夫人玉鬘，对于太政大臣家诸公子，即她的异母兄弟柏木等，不甚亲近，

en.t: Now Tamakazura, the wife of the Left General Higekuro, was not very close to the young gentlemen of the Chancellor's household, that is, to her half brothers such as Kashiwagi,

units.source_text: 而对于右大将夕雾，反而亲近，同从前住在六条院时一样。

en.t: but she was quite intimate with the Right General Yugiri, just as she had been when she lived at Rokujo-in in former days.

units.source_text: 这玉鬘富有才气，且又和蔼可亲。

en.t: Tamakazura was gifted and intelligent, and also gentle and approachable.

units.source_text: 她每次和夕雾见面，总是热诚招待，毫无疏远之色。

en.t: Whenever she met Yugiri, she always received him warmly and showed not the slightest sign of distance.

units.source_text: 夕雾也觉得异母妹淑景舍女御不易接近，态度过分冷淡，反不如玉鬘之和蔼可亲。

en.t: Yugiri, too, felt that his half sister, the Shokyoden Consort, was hard to approach and far too cold in manner, and that she could not compare with Tamakazura's kindness and warmth.

units.source_text: 因此夕雾与玉鬘保持一种既非手足、又非恋人的特殊爱情，两人互相亲善。

en.t: Thus Yugiri and Tamakazura maintained a special affection that was neither sibling love nor romance, and the two remained warmly attached to each other.

units.source_text: 而髭黑大将现在已和前妻式部卿亲王的女儿完全断绝关系，对玉鬘的宠爱也无以复加。

en.t: Meanwhile, General Higekuro had by now completely severed his ties with his former wife, the daughter of Prince Shikibukyo, and his devotion to Tamakazura could not have been greater.

units.source_text: 惟玉鬘所生两个孩子，都是男的，家中没有女儿，未免寂寞，因此想把前妻所生女儿真木柱接来，归自己抚养。

en.t: However, the two children born to Tamakazura were both boys, and since there was no daughter in the household, he felt it rather lonely and wished to bring over Makibashira, the daughter of his former wife, and raise her himself.

units.source_text: 但真木柱的外祖父式部卿亲王坚决不许，他想：“我至少要把这外孙女好好地抚养成人，不使她让人贻笑大方。”

en.t: But Makibashira's maternal grandfather, Prince Shikibukyo, firmly refused, thinking, “At the very least, I must raise this granddaughter properly and not let her become a laughingstock.”

units.source_text: 对人也常如此说。

en.t: He often said the same thing to others as well.

units.source_text: 这位亲王确实声望隆盛。

en.t: This prince truly enjoyed great prestige and renown.

units.source_text: 冷泉帝对这位舅父也非常尊重，但凡有所奏请，无不照准，以为不准是对他不起的。

en.t: Emperor Reizei also held this uncle in very high respect, and whenever the prince made a request, he granted it, feeling that to refuse would be an offense against him.

units.source_text: 这位亲王素来是个爱好时髦的人，其阔绰仅次于源氏和太政大臣。

en.t: This prince had always been a man who loved refinement and fashion, and his lavish style was second only to Genji and the Chancellor.

units.source_text: 家里出入的人甚多，世人对他也十分重视。

en.t: Many people came and went at his residence, and society at large regarded him with great importance.

units.source_text: 髭黑大将将来可为天下柱石，现在是个候补者。

en.t: General Higekuro was a man who might one day become a pillar of the realm, and for now he was a likely candidate for such a role.

units.source_text: 真木柱有那样的外祖父和这样的父亲，其声望岂有不高贵之理！

en.t: With such a grandfather and such a father, how could Makibashira's standing be anything but noble and distinguished?

units.source_text: 因此远远近近，求婚之人甚多，但式部卿亲王尚未选定。

en.t: For that reason, many suitors came from near and far, but Prince Shikibukyo had not yet made his choice.

units.source_text: 他心中思忖：如果柏木卫门督前来求婚，倒可以允许他。

en.t: In his heart he thought that if Kashiwagi, the Gate Guards Captain, were to come seeking her hand, he might well allow it.

units.source_text: 而柏木呢，大概认为真木柱不如小猫吧，全然不曾想到这条路，真乃遗憾之事。

en.t: As for Kashiwagi, perhaps he thought Makibashira inferior even to a kitten, for he never considered that path at all, which was truly a pity.

units.source_text: 真木柱看见自己的生母为人一直怪里怪气，疯头疯脑，全无常人模样，几乎脱离人世，觉得真可痛惜；

en.t: Makibashira saw that her own mother had long been strange and unbalanced, with no trace of ordinary human composure and almost withdrawn from the world, and she found it deeply painful;

units.source_text: 而对于继母玉鬘的风度，则非常羡慕，很想来依附她。

en.t: but she greatly admired the bearing of her stepmother Tamakazura and very much wished to come and depend on her.

units.source_text: 原来真木柱也是个心爱时髦阔绰的人。

en.t: Makibashira herself, after all, was also someone who loved fashion, elegance, and splendor.
